title: Why Costco Sells Hot Dogs for $1.50

research.centralQuestion: Why has Costco refused to raise the $1.50 hot dog price since the mid-1980s?
research.businessMechanism: Costco's retail merchandise is sold near cost; over 52% of total operating income is generated entirely by recurring annual membership card fees ($4.8 billion in 2024).

verifiedFacts.claim: Costco hot dog combo has remained $1.50 since the mid-1980s, selling nearly 200 million annually.
In FY2024 Costco collected $4.8 billion in membership fees, accounting for 52% of operating income.

doNotClaim: Do not state exact margin or loss on individual hot dog combos as Costco does not disclose item-level margins.
Do not give an exact launch year; say only 'mid-1980s'.
Do not compare fees to net income; compare to operating income only.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: Every time inflation hits, food prices double. But Costco's hot dog has stayed one dollar and fifty cents since the mid-nineteen eighties. How do they not go broke?

dialogue.speaker: insider
dialogue.text: Because you aren't paying for the hot dog. You're paying for permission to buy it.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: Wait... they sell nearly two hundred million hot dogs just to get us in the door?

dialogue.speaker: insider
dialogue.text: The hot dog is just the bait. In twenty twenty-four, Costco collected four point eight billion dollars purely in membership fees. That card is fifty-two percent of their entire operating income.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: So Costco makes over half their operating profit before selling a single item.

dialogue.speaker: insider
dialogue.text: Costco is a private subscription club that happens to have pallets of paper towels in the back.
